data.exact_reserve_text: Reserves established in 2017 and 2018 in respect of the Atlantic basin hurricanes, Californian wildfires and Japanese typhoons have, in aggregate, proved to be broadly adequate. Adverse development on Hurricane Michael and Typhoon Jebi has been offset by favourable development elsewhere. Much of the adverse development has been absorbed into the retrocession in place; some of the reductions have delivered a net benefit.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's gross claims reserves at 1 January 2019 were GBP 1,215.8m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates an overall favourable prior-year development of approximately GBP 56.8m (around 4.7% of opening gross reserves), driven by favourable run-off across several older years. This net release masks adverse development on specific prior events (notably Hurricane Michael and Typhoon Jebi) which was largely absorbed by retrocession, and favourable development on other Atlantic hurricanes, Californian wildfires and Japanese typhoons. Reserves were set conservatively and the syndicate reports that the prior year strengthening in some areas was offset by releases elsewhere.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development extracted by summing changes from the gross claims development triangle (gross values) for underwriting years up to 2017. The syndicate undertook a reinsurance-to-close of Syndicate 2255 into Syndicate 435 on 1 January 2018; this RITC (noted elsewhere in the report) may distort 2018 comparatives and the triangle. Figures in the accounts and triangle are presented in GBP '000; triangle-based PYD therefore computed from those values (converted to GBP m). No explicit single-note 'movement in prior year's provision' gross figure was provided; triangle used as primary gross source.
